problem: Existing embodied navigation datasets (Gibson, MP3D, HM3D) mostly contain cluttered houses and offices with short episodes, so occupancy-based agents are never tested in large, uncluttered spaces with sparse occupancy cues and very long paths.
motivation: Scene variety limits what agents learn and how they are evaluated. A museum has large rooms, many visually unique points of interest and sparse occupancy, which stresses depth-reliant mapping and pose estimation and exposes error accumulation over long trajectories.
key_idea: Release a Matterport-scanned 3D art gallery (AG3D) with exploration episodes and a PointGoal++ (position plus final orientation) navigation benchmark with long geodesic paths, and benchmark existing modular exploration/navigation agents on it.
insight: Agents trained only on Gibson transfer poorly. Finetuning on AG3D helps in both tasks: in noisy PointNav, Coverage on Gibson+AG3D reaches SPL 0.373 vs 0.228 for Gibson-only. Noise-free vs noisy PointNav SPL drops sharply (0.805 to 0.235 for the scratch model), showing that long AG3D episodes expose accumulating pose error. Scratch training on AG3D wins in noise-free PointNav, but finetuning is more robust under noise.
method: Dataset acquisition: 232 Matterport Pro2 panoramic RGB-D scans about 1.5 m apart at Galleria Estense (Modena), giving over 1430 m² navigable space.
Exploration episodes: 500k train / 100 val / 1000 test episodes with start poses sampled uniformly over the navigable space.

PointGoal++ benchmark: 147 annotated points of interest (paintings, statues), goal about 1 m in front of the artwork with orientation towards its center; 3 episodes per point (easy <15 m, medium >15 m, difficult >30 m), 411 episodes in total.

Mapper: ResNet-18+UNet on RGB and UNet on depth fused by CNNs, decoded to a 101x101 local occupancy/explored map (5 cm cells) that also anticipates occluded areas, registered into a 2881x2881 global map.
Pose estimator: a CNN refines noisy sensor displacement using consecutive local maps.

Hierarchical policy: PPO global policy (Coverage, Anticipation or Curiosity reward) picks a goal on a 240x240 grid; an A* planner sets local goals; a local RL policy outputs forward 0.25 m / turn 10° / stop.
Evaluation protocol: Gibson-trained baselines (~5M frames) vs scratch on AG3D (~2.8M frames) vs Gibson finetuned on AG3D (+~1M frames), with noise-free and noisy settings.

setting.backbone: Modular ResNet-18/UNet mapper + CNN pose estimator + PPO global and local policies (trained from scratch or finetuned)
setting.training_data: Gibson (~5M frames, 12 GPU-days on V100) for baselines; AG3D exploration episodes (~2.8M frames from scratch, or ~1M frames finetuning)
setting.observation: 128x128 egocentric RGB-D plus pose sensor (noise-free or noisy)
setting.action_space: low-level: move forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 10°, stop (navigation only)
setting.privileged: none (GT map only used for exploration reward/metrics)

results: On AG3D, Gibson-only agents perform poorly, and adapting to AG3D helps. Coverage finetuned on Gibson+AG3D gives the best exploration (noise-free IoU 0.296 vs 0.214 for Gibson-only Coverage). In PointGoal++, noise-free SPL is 0.805 with scratch training, while in noisy conditions finetuning reaches SPL 0.373 vs 0.228 for Gibson-only Coverage.
limitations: Small benchmark: a single building, 411 navigation episodes and 100 validation exploration episodes, with only three variants of one modular architecture evaluated.
Scratch vs finetuned comparisons are confounded by unequal training frames (2.8M vs 6M total), and no learning-free or end-to-end baselines are included.
Noisy PointNav collapses (SR ~0.25-0.40), so it is unclear whether the failure is caused by the pose estimator or the scene; no real-robot validation.
